paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption_used: Distribution of articles across the three-year collection period (2017-2019), displayed as a pie chart with percentage and count labels. The 2019 cohort (blue) represents the largest share at 46.0% (46 articles), followed by 2018 (orange) at 33.0% (33 articles) and 2017 (green) at 21.0% (21 articles). The distribution reflects a steady annual increase, with the 2018-to-2019 growth rate of approximately 25% exceeding the 2017-to-2018 growth rate of roughly 35%. The combined 2017-2018 corpus accounts for slightly over half of all articles at 54%, suggesting that the collection effort intensified primarily in the final year.

model_annotations.English: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of articles across the three-year collection period from 2017 to 2019, divided into three distinct slices corresponding to each year: 2017 is shown in green, 2018 in orange, and 2019 in blue. The largest segment, colored blue and labeled “2019,” accounts for 46.0% (46 articles), followed by the orange “2018” segment at 33.0% (33 articles), and the green “2017” segment at 21.0% (21 articles). Each slice is clearly labeled with its respective year, percentage, and absolute count in parentheses. The chart includes percentage labels directly within each segment and does not use a separate legend, as the colors and labels are sufficient to identify each year. The segments are arranged in descending order of size, with 2019 at the top, 2018 to its lower left, and 2017 to its lower right, forming a clockwise progression. No slices are visually emphasized or exploded from the chart’s center.
